Release Checklist

This file exercises the title-line heuristic: a short capitalized line with no
trailing punctuation, surrounded by blank lines, is treated as a section break.

Build The Wheel

Run the packaging job and confirm the artifact hash matches the one recorded in
the release notes. If it does not, stop and investigate before tagging.

===

lowercase heading is not a boundary

A line that starts lowercase is left inside the previous section, and so is a
line that ends with punctuation, because the heuristic requires a capital start
and no trailing period.

This line is far too long to be treated as a section title because it runs well
past the one hundred character limit the heuristic enforces on candidate lines.

# Hash Marks Start A Section

Any line beginning with a hash is a boundary regardless of length or case. That
covers Markdown headers and shell comments alike, which is why a source file
full of comments fragments into many sections.

Final Notes

Dr. Knuth wrote about literate programming. He argued that a program should be
written for a human reader first, e.g. as an essay, and only incidentally for
the machine. That argument applies to chunking too: the cut points should fall
where a human would pause, not where a byte counter happens to land.
